title: Dimensions of data quality: accuracy, completeness, consistency and timeliness

videos.script: A grocer asks a simple question. How much did we sell in 2025? The database answers at once, to the centavo. {{answer}} And the number is wrong. Not wildly wrong. Wrong by a few repeated orders, a few totals typed with an extra zero, a bag of sugar charged at more than ten times its price. Nothing on the screen says so. {{nothing-says}} This course is about that gap. Between a query that runs and an answer you can defend. {{gap}} It starts by naming what can go wrong. A value can be accurate or not. A column can be complete or full of holes. Two files can agree, or contradict each other. And a file can simply be old. {{dimensions}} Each of those is a question you can turn into a rule. And each rule gives you a number. {{rules}} In this lesson you build the machine every other lesson runs on. You open the files. And you measure how dirty they are, with six rules and six numbers. {{scorecard}} The cleaning starts in lesson 2. First, find out what you are dealing with. {{end}}
